word:hebrew:H1060.explanation: Bekowr means firstborn. It can also mean chief, as in the chiefs among Esau’s sons.

word:hebrew:H1129.explanation: Bânâh means to build. It can describe building an altar or a house.

word:hebrew:H1165.explanation: Bᵉʻîyr means cattle or beast. It can refer to animals loaded for travel or grazing in a field.

word:hebrew:H1262.explanation: Bârah means to choose. It can also describe eating.

word:hebrew:H135.explanation: Addan is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H1367.explanation: Gebuwlah means a boundary or region. It can describe land marked out by its borders.

word:hebrew:H1473.explanation: Golah means exile. It can also refer collectively to exiles—people who have been carried away and are in captivity.

word:hebrew:H1499.explanation: This Hebrew word means “violent,” describing something marked by violence. It functions as a description of harmful conduct or conditions, rather than naming a person or place. In the Old Testament, it occurs two times: once in Ecclesiastes and once in Ezekiel. Its use in both passages presents violence as a serious wrong associated with injustice and death, while the surrounding verse determines the precise force of the description.

word:hebrew:H1536.explanation: This Hebrew word means “wheel,” referring to a round object used in movement or work. It functions as a noun and appears once in the Hebrew Bible, in Isaiah 28:28. Its precise role there depends on the surrounding verse and passage, but the word itself names the wheel rather than an action or quality. The repeated rendering “wheel” supports this basic meaning without requiring additional translation senses.

word:hebrew:H1730.explanation: Dôwd can mean love. It can also refer to a beloved person. In a family relationship, it specifically means an uncle.

word:hebrew:H179.explanation: Obil is a personal name identifying an Ishmaelite.

word:hebrew:H1842.explanation: Dan-Jaan is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H1907.explanation: Haddâbâr means a vizier, or counsellor serving a king.

word:hebrew:H193.explanation: ʼUwl can mean powerful or mighty. It is also rendered as strength.

word:hebrew:H1990.explanation: Ham means a region of Palestine. Chedorlaomer and the kings with him struck the Rephaim there.

word:hebrew:H2047.explanation: Hathak is the name of a Persian eunuch.

word:hebrew:H207.explanation: This Hebrew word is the name “Ono,” referring to a place rather than expressing an action, quality, or abstract idea. It functions as a geographical proper name in these passages. It appears five times in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, and each recorded rendering is “Ono.” The name occurs in 1 Chronicles 8:12, Ezra 2:33, and Nehemiah 6:2, 7:37, and 11:35. Its precise significance in any passage comes from the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H2146.explanation: Zikrown means a memorial: something kept to remember.

word:hebrew:H2201.explanation: Zaʻaq means a cry or outcry.

word:hebrew:H2238.explanation: Zeresh is the name of Haman’s wife.

word:hebrew:H23.explanation: Abiasaph is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H2353.explanation: This Hebrew word describes something white, or something made of linen. It appears twice in the Old Testament, both times in Esther, where English renderings use “white” and “linen.” Thus, its central sense concerns a light-colored appearance or linen material, depending on how it functions in the sentence. The surrounding wording determines whether the emphasis falls on color or on the fabric itself. Its occurrences are Esther 1:6 and Esther 8:15.

word:hebrew:H2432.explanation: Hilen is a Hebrew proper name used to identify a particular named entity rather than express an action, quality, or general idea. It is rendered “Hilen” in the available English renderings. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 1 Chronicles 6:58. Without the surrounding verse text, its precise referent cannot be described further, but its function is that of a name rather than an ordinary descriptive term.

word:hebrew:H2586.explanation: Chanun is a personal name, rendered Hanun; one Hanun was the son of the king of Ammon.

word:hebrew:H2649.explanation: Chippazon means haste, especially a hurried departure.

word:hebrew:H2740.explanation: Charon means a burning of anger, expressed as wrath.

word:hebrew:H2869.explanation: Tab means good. It can also describe something fine, as with fine gold.

word:hebrew:H2883.explanation: Taba means to sink, as when someone goes down into deep mire or water without any firm footing.

word:hebrew:H2937.explanation: Ta'a means to lead astray or seduce.

word:hebrew:H3170.explanation: Yachzerah is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H3233.explanation: This Hebrew word means “right.” It functions as a directional word, identifying the right side or position rather than expressing an action or quality by itself. It occurs 33 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, including repeated use in Leviticus and occurrences in Exodus, Kings, Chronicles, and Ezekiel. Its precise force in any particular verse depends on the surrounding sentence, but its central meaning remains the designation of what is right.

word:hebrew:H3318.explanation: Yatsa means to go out or bring something out. It describes Zebulun’s going out and Yahweh bringing Israel out of Egypt.

word:hebrew:H3321.explanation: This Hebrew word means “truth.” It names or describes truth within its sentence, serving as the word’s central lexical idea rather than expressing an action or command. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, at Daniel 7:19. Because the verse text and wider context are not included here, this cache identifies the word’s ordinary meaning and function without assigning a more specific emphasis to that verse.

word:hebrew:H3354.explanation: Jekuthiel is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than describing an action, quality, or object. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in 1 Chronicles 4:18, within a genealogical setting. The name is rendered "Jekuthiel," and its precise significance beyond this name form is not established by the available lexical information. Its role in the passage is therefore to identify a person recorded in the genealogy.

word:hebrew:H3417.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to spit—the act or substance of spitting. It occurs three times in the Old Testament Hebrew corpus, in two verses: twice in Numbers 12:14 and once in Deuteronomy 25:9. In each setting, the word describes spitting as an outward physical act. Its use in these passages keeps the meaning concrete rather than presenting an abstract idea. The precise force of the act in either verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself means “spit.”

word:hebrew:H342.explanation: Eibah means hostility, enmity, or hatred.

word:hebrew:H3480.explanation: Jesharelah is a Hebrew personal name. It functions as a proper name, identifying an individual rather than expressing a general action, quality, or object. This name occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 1 Chronicles 25:14, and the English rendering preserves it as “Jesharelah.” Without the surrounding verse text, no further contextual significance should be assigned to the name itself.

word:hebrew:H3563.explanation: Kôs means a cup or container. It can also refer to an owl.

word:hebrew:H3589.explanation: Kiyd means a crushing; figuratively, calamity or destruction.

word:hebrew:H3619.explanation: Keluwb means a cage. It can also mean a basket.

word:hebrew:H3655.explanation: Kanah means to give someone an additional name or surname. It can also describe giving flattering titles.

word:hebrew:H3772.explanation: Kârath means to cut, including cutting something down or cutting something off. It can also describe destroying something. It can also mean making a covenant or alliance.

word:hebrew:H3813.explanation: This Hebrew word means “covered.” It functions as the predicate in its one Old Testament occurrence, describing what is done or what condition applies. The word appears only once, in 2 Samuel 19:4, so its broader range of use cannot be established from repeated biblical examples. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding verse text and passage context, but “covered” is the supported ordinary meaning.

word:hebrew:H3934.explanation: Laʻeg means a buffoon or mocker. It can also describe stammering.

word:hebrew:H3941.explanation: “Lappidoth” is a personal name identifying an individual in the Hebrew Old Testament. It appears only once, in Judges 4:4, so its basic function is to identify a person rather than describe an action, quality, or object. The name is connected in the SEE record with the Hebrew entities for Israel and judge at that reference, but the available information does not provide enough verse text to explain the person’s specific role or significance there.

word:hebrew:H3978.explanation: Ma'akāl means food or something edible.

word:hebrew:H3996.explanation: Mabo means an entrance or entry. It can also refer to sunset, the going down of the sun.

word:hebrew:H4063.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “garments” and refers to articles worn by a person. It occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, once in 2 Samuel 10:4 and once in 1 Chronicles 19:4. In both places, it names garments as a concrete object, functioning as the thing involved in the sentence rather than describing an action, person, or quality. Its basic sense is therefore straightforward: garments. It identifies what is worn.

word:hebrew:H4089.explanation: Madmannah is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H4117.explanation: This Hebrew verb means “endow,” expressing an action of granting or assigning something. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both occurrences within Exodus 22:16. Because the available wording is limited and no verse text is provided here, the word’s precise force in that passage depends on its surrounding context. Its role is verbal: it describes what someone does rather than naming a person, object, or quality.

word:hebrew:H412.explanation: This Hebrew word means “these,” pointing to particular people or things already identified in the surrounding statement. It functions as a demonstrative expression, directing attention to more than one item rather than naming or describing those items themselves. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus represented here, it occurs twice, both occurrences appearing in Ezra 5:15. Its exact reference depends on the surrounding verse, but its basic role is to identify a specific group or set as “these.”

word:hebrew:H4180.explanation: Mowrash means a possession. It can also refer to thoughts.

word:hebrew:H4272.explanation: Machats means to dash asunder—to crush or smash with force.

word:hebrew:H4319.explanation: This word is a Hebrew personal name, not a common word describing an action, quality, or object. It occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in Judges 17. The available references identify its use in that passage, but no explicit definition or approved meaning term is available here. Therefore, its dependable role is to identify the person named, while the surrounding verse supplies the details of his actions and significance.

word:hebrew:H4355.explanation: Mâkak means to tumble into ruins or perish, including being brought low. It can also describe something decaying.

word:hebrew:H4618.explanation: Maʻănâh means a furrow, the mark made when soil is plowed.

word:hebrew:H4621.explanation: Maʻătsâd means an axe. It can also mean tongs, a smith’s tool.

word:hebrew:H4654.explanation: Mappalah means a ruin or something fallen.

word:hebrew:H4795.explanation: This Hebrew word means “purification.” It names an act or process rather than a person, place, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, it occurs once, in Esther 2:12. Because no broader range of uses is recorded, its central idea remains this focused term. The word itself supplies the idea of purification; it does not, by itself, establish every detail surrounding that act.

word:hebrew:H4856.explanation: This Hebrew word means “respect,” naming the quality or attitude of showing respect toward someone. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in 2 Chronicles 19:7, so its recorded use is limited to that single passage. In the sentence, it functions as the thing connected with the action or attitude being described. The surrounding verse determines exactly how this respect is expressed there.

word:hebrew:H4975.explanation: Môthen means the waist or small of the back; in the plural, it refers to the loins.

word:hebrew:H5020.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar is the personal name of the king of Babylon.

word:hebrew:H508.explanation: This Hebrew word is a personal name, rendered “Elpaal.” It identifies a man in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles 8 rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. The name occurs three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, all within that chapter: 1 Chronicles 8:11, 8:12, and 8:18. Its repeated appearance connects it with family lineage and genealogical relationships. The available information supports understanding it as the proper name of a person, while the name’s deeper meaning is not established here.

word:hebrew:H5114.explanation: Nodab is a Hebrew personal name, preserved as a proper name rather than an ordinary descriptive word. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in 1 Chronicles 5:19, and the English renderings retain it as “Nodab.” Because no explicit definition or surrounding verse text is available here, its lexical meaning cannot be stated beyond its function as a name. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H5158.explanation: Nachal means a stream or brook, especially a winter torrent. It can also refer to a narrow valley.

word:hebrew:H5161.explanation: Nehelamite means a descendant of Nechlam.

word:hebrew:H5222.explanation: Nêkeh means a smiter—an attacker. Here it is rendered “abjects” for people who gathered against the speaker and tore at him.

word:hebrew:H531.explanation: Amots is the name of an Israelite, known in English as Amoz.

word:hebrew:H5327.explanation: Natsah means to quarrel or strive with others.

word:hebrew:H544.explanation: This word expresses a limited idea whose exact sense depends on its context. It appears only once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Isaiah 25:1, so its meaning cannot be established broadly from repeated biblical usage. No concise English meaning or definition is available here. The surrounding verse would be needed to explain precisely what the word contributes to the sentence. Its recorded relationship in that verse places it among actions directed toward God, but the bare reference does not provide enough context to state more. word:hebrew:H5477.explanation: Suah is a Hebrew personal name, rendered as “Suah.” It identifies an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or abstract idea. This name occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, at 1 Chronicles 7:36. Without the surrounding verse text, no further contextual significance should be assigned to the name itself. Its ordinary lexical function is simply to designate the person called Suah.

word:hebrew:H5626.explanation: Sirah is a proper name, identifying a particular place or person rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 2 Samuel 3:26, and is rendered “Sirah.” Because the available biblical wording does not provide a descriptive definition, the name itself is the clearest supported meaning. Its precise referent belongs to the surrounding verse and passage, not to the name alone.

word:hebrew:H5684.explanation: This Hebrew word is the place-name “Ebronah,” referring to a location rather than describing an action, quality, or object. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in Numbers 33:34–35. Since it functions as a name, its meaning for readers is mainly identification: it tells us which place is being named. The surrounding verse context determines what is being said about Ebronah in each occurrence.

word:hebrew:H5811.explanation: Azaz is a Hebrew name rendered “Azaz,” functioning as a personal designation rather than a translated descriptive word. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in 1 Chronicles 5:8. Because it is preserved as a name, its meaning here is chiefly identification: it distinguishes the person named from others in the passage. The surrounding verse would be needed to explain that person’s specific role or significance.

word:hebrew:H5864.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to a place named “Iim.” It functions as a proper place-name rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. The name appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, once in Numbers 33:45 and once in Joshua 15:29. Since no lexical definition is given, its supported meaning is limited to identifying this place. The surrounding verse text is needed to explain the location’s role in each passage.

word:hebrew:H6007.explanation: “Amasiah” is a personal name, identifying one individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or object. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in 2 Chronicles 17:16. Because the available rendering preserves it as a name, its ordinary function is to identify the person named in that passage. The name itself does not provide enough information here to explain the person’s character, role, or significance without the surrounding verse text.

word:hebrew:H603.explanation: Anāqah means shrieking, crying out, groaning, or sighing.

word:hebrew:H6090.explanation: ʻOtseb means a fashioned idol or pain of body or mind, including sorrow. It can also describe something wicked.

word:hebrew:H6142.explanation: Ikkesh is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H6216.explanation: This Hebrew noun means an “oppressor,” referring to someone who treats others harshly or unjustly through power or control. It identifies the wrongdoer rather than the person suffering under that treatment. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Jeremiah 22:3, and its use there belongs to a spoken command involving the removal of oppressive wrongdoing. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H6335.explanation: Pûwsh means to spread or be scattered. Figuratively, it can describe acting proudly.

word:hebrew:H6379.explanation: This Hebrew word describes an action or condition in Ezekiel 47:2, but the available material does not provide a gloss or approved meaning term for translating it more precisely. It appears only once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus and functions as the predicate in its recorded relationships. Its exact sense must therefore be determined from the verse’s actual wording and surrounding context, rather than from this word record alone.

word:hebrew:H6393.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “torches,” or objects used to provide visible flame or light. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Nahum 2:3. Because no explicit definition or verse text is available here, its ordinary meaning is best stated from that approved rendering alone. The word functions as a noun, naming the torches themselves rather than an action or quality. Its precise significance in Nahum 2:3 depends on the surrounding verse and passage, which must be considered separately.

word:hebrew:H6403.explanation: Pâlaṭ means to slip out or escape. It can also mean to deliver someone.

word:hebrew:H6582.explanation: Pashach means to tear in pieces.

word:hebrew:H6612.explanation: Pethiy means simple or easily led. In Scripture, it can describe someone lacking understanding, and the simple are called to understand wisdom.

word:hebrew:H6708.explanation: This Hebrew word is a rare term whose ordinary meaning cannot be established from the available lexical information alone. It occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in Nehemiah 4:13, but the verse text and English rendering are not available here to clarify its sense. Its recorded lemma is צְחִיחִי. The surrounding passage would be needed to explain precisely what the term describes in that occurrence.

word:hebrew:H6731.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to a flower or blossom, and it can describe a flower-shaped ornament or a natural bloom. In the Old Testament, it occurs 15 times, including descriptions of the priestly headpiece, Aaron’s blossoming rod, and flower designs in the temple. Its normal sense centers on something that blossoms or has the appearance of a flower, while the surrounding sentence identifies whether it is a living plant or a crafted decoration. References include Exod. 28:36, Num. 17:8, and 1 Kgs. 6:18. word:hebrew:H6744.explanation: Tsᵉlach means to advance. It can describe work that prospers and people who are promoted.

word:hebrew:H6829.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “Zaphon,” a place name rather than a general description or action. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Joshua 13:27, and both recorded English renderings preserve it as “Zaphon.” Because no verse text or surrounding passage is provided here, the word’s normal lexical function can be stated clearly, but its precise significance in that location must be understood from the surrounding passage. It functions as a proper name identifying a specific place.

word:hebrew:H6865.explanation: Tsôr names a place in Palestine, rendered in English as Tyre or Tyrus.

word:hebrew:H6960.explanation: Qavah means to bind together or gather. It can also mean to wait or expect.

word:hebrew:H7039.explanation: Qali means roasted ears of grain, or parched grain.

word:hebrew:H7075.explanation: Qinyân means goods or possessions—what someone owns or has acquired.

word:hebrew:H7156.explanation: Qiryathayim is a place-name used for two places in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H7181.explanation: Qashab means to listen attentively—to hearken, heed, or give ear.

word:hebrew:H7350.explanation: Rachowq means far away, remote, or distant. It can also describe figurative distance, as in being far from help.

word:hebrew:H7413.explanation: Ramah means a height or high place.

word:hebrew:H7534.explanation: This Hebrew word describes something “thin,” indicating a lack of thickness or fullness. It is used in the Old Testament three times, all within Genesis 41, where it functions as a descriptive word for the condition of something. Its meaning remains focused and concrete: the subject is thin rather than substantial or full-bodied. The surrounding verse determines exactly what is being described, but the word itself supplies this basic description.

word:hebrew:H7541.explanation: Raqqah means the temple, the side of the head.

word:hebrew:H7596.explanation: She'elah means a petition. It can also refer to a loan.

word:hebrew:H7606.explanation: She'ar means the rest, or a residue.

word:hebrew:H7817.explanation: Shachach means to sink or be brought low. It can also describe bowing down or stooping.

word:hebrew:H782.explanation: Aresheth means a longing for. It can also refer to a request.

word:hebrew:H7880.explanation: Siyach means a shoot or shrubbery, referring to a bush or plant.

word:hebrew:H7963.explanation: This Hebrew word means “tranquillity.” It functions as a term naming a settled condition, rather than an action or person. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Daniel 4:27. Because the verse text and surrounding passage are not included here, the word’s precise force in that sentence must be understood from its context, while its basic lexical sense remains tranquillity.

word:hebrew:H7989.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to a governor or ruler—someone who possesses power and authority. It can describe a person who governs others, as well as the power or strength associated with ruling. The word appears four times in the Hebrew Old Testament: once in Genesis and three times in Ecclesiastes. Its central idea is authority exercised over others, whether viewed through the ruler himself or through the power that enables him to rule.

word:hebrew:H8049.explanation: Shamhuth is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H8232.explanation: This Hebrew word means “be,” expressing existence or a state of being. It functions as a verb, describing what someone or something is or comes to be rather than naming a person, object, or quality. It occurs three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, all in Daniel. Its exact force in each passage depends on the surrounding sentence, but its basic role is to indicate being or existence.

word:hebrew:H8324.explanation: Sharar means to be hostile, as an enemy or opponent.

word:hebrew:H8368.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to something secret or hidden from ordinary view. It functions as a verb, describing an action rather than naming a person, place, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs only once, at 1 Samuel 5:9, so its broader range cannot be established from repeated biblical usage. The available rendering supports the meaning “secret,” while the exact force of the word in that verse depends on the surrounding verse text and context.

word:hebrew:H8401.explanation: Teben means straw or stubble—the leftover stalks of grain.

word:hebrew:H8438.explanation: The Hebrew word refers to “scarlet,” identifying a scarlet color or material in a passage. It occurs 43 times in the Hebrew Old Testament. Many occurrences are connected with making or describing the tabernacle’s curtains and garments, showing its frequent use for crafted sacred items. Other passages use it in different settings, so the surrounding wording determines exactly what bears this scarlet quality. Its ordinary function is to identify something as scarlet within the sentence.

word:hebrew:H8474.explanation: Tacharâh means to vie with a rival, or to contend.

word:hebrew:H85.explanation: Abraham is the later name of Abram.

word:hebrew:H8553.explanation: Timnah is a proper place name, referring to a location called “Timnah.” It is not a general word describing an object, action, or quality, but the name of a specific place mentioned in the Old Testament. The name appears 12 times in the Hebrew corpus, including references in Genesis, Joshua, Judges, and 2 Chronicles. Its precise significance in any particular verse comes from the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H8647.explanation: “Tirhanah” is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than describing an action or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in 1 Chronicles 2:48, within a genealogical record. Its role there is to identify a person connected with a birth or family line. Because the word is a proper name, its meaning is primarily its identifying function; the surrounding genealogy supplies its significance in that passage.

word:hebrew:H867.explanation: Ethni is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears only once, in 1 Chronicles 6:41, and the English rendering preserves it as “Ethni.” Because the available information identifies this word chiefly as a name and does not provide a separate definition, its normal meaning is the person’s name itself. Its specific role in that verse depends on the surrounding genealogy and passage context.

word:hebrew:H962.explanation: Bâzaz means to plunder or spoil. It describes taking plunder from cities, as the children of Israel did.
